Vuelta 2026: Favourites

fotobureau Cor VosFreddy Maertens won thirteen stages in the 1977 Vuelta a España. With three wins in five stages, Tadej Pogacar was well on his way to challenging that record, but he was forced to abandon in stage 8 after a crash. What can we expect over the coming stages? So far, Matthew Brennan has claimed three stage wins and Wout van Aert two, while Marco Brenner, Andreas Leknessund, Bryan Coquard, Enric Mas and Bastien Tronchon have all tasted stage success once.

Read about themain contenders to win La Vuelta.

For sprinters and attackers

In any other Grand Tour, Stage 16 would be a nailed-on sprint finish, but that remains to be seen at the Vuelta. For starters, there aren’t that many fast finishers in the race, and it is uncertain how many of them will still be in Spain by the third week? So, who is going to keep the breakaway under control?
Read more »

Rollings roads towards sprint finish

The 15th stage of the Vuelta is a rolling affair until the Puerto Artafi spices up the final 30 kilometres with a 5.9-kilometre climb averaging 5.6%. There’s a good chance the more resilient sprinters in the Vuelta a España will have no trouble getting over it and will battle it out for the win in Córdoba.
Read more »

For fast men #4

Stage 17 is the flattest stage of the Vuelta, and it would be a major surprise if the sprinters don’t have the final say.
Read more »

Another feast for the climbers

It's back to the climbers on La Vuelta's 14th stage. After spending the entire day riding either uphill or downhill, the riders face an average gradient of 7.2% over the final 11.9 kilometres in the Sierra de la Pandera.
Read more »

For fast-finishing attackers

It is neither the first nor the last time in this Vuelta that the riders face a stage with a hilly opening section and a relatively flat second half. Sprinters or attackers, or - maybe even better - a combination of both?
Read more »
